brief: Pasquariello sets the scale first. Hyperscaler capex was $154bn in 2023 and consensus for 2028 is over $1.3tr, so the market is right to focus on return on invested capital, and the bar for tying that spend to durable revenue growth has risen. Hyperscaler results delivered moments of that proof in 2026, META in Q4, GOOG and AMZN in Q1, MSFT and AMZN in Q2, but the buzz faded each time. He therefore argues binary ROIC framing is too reductive. The payoff may instead be enterprise value created when businesses of all sizes operate better, with cloud spending as the analogy, plus compulsory AI spend to protect a business, with cyber as the analogy. Because adoption is early, precise ROIC is not calculable. If those notions hold, Corporate America keeps spending, including low or no ROI spend born of necessity. Against that he flags gathering risks, the political dynamics with midterms as a litmus test on cost bearing, malevolence, and a lack of power provision. His conclusion is that the secular AI spending trend stays intact and structurally higher, but the path is more jagged, with rising risk of air pockets akin to DeepSeek.
